reading_head: The Distance Between a Fact and a Verdict
reading_sub: Questions first, then the text. Use the glossary.

paras: An investigation is not a court. Its report can say what happened, but it rarely says that a person was negligent. Negligence is a legal decision, and only a court can make it.

Look at three sentences about the same fact. The valve was closed. It would appear that the valve was closed. The witness stated that he had closed the valve. Only the first is a finding: the report is sure. The second is a hedge: the evidence points to it, but it is not certain. The third is testimony: it is only what a person said.

Investigators are careful. More often than not, a root cause is first written as a contributing factor. It becomes a root cause only after the corrective action is agreed. Investigators would rather say too little than too much, because a strong finding that is wrong can destroy the whole report.
The advice to young investigators is simple. If two explanations are possible, you had better write both. If you can test one of them, you may as well test it first.

listenings.sub: A senior investigator explains why she writes carefully. Sound first, no text.
listenings.text: In thirty years, two of my findings were overturned. I remember them better than anything I got right. In both cases the fact was correct, but my sentence was too strong. When you write that a person was negligent, you are not describing an event any more. You are making a legal claim, and somebody will test it. So I write it would appear that. Some people say that is weak. It is not weak. It is honest about how much I know. If the evidence gets stronger later, I can make the sentence stronger. And there is a second reason. A careful finding is easier for the company to accept.

pc_desc: The words of an official inquiry and the hedges that show if a text states or only suggests. Key words: negligence, testimony, investigation, finding, recommendation, contributing factor, root cause, corrective action, witness, sequence of events. Structure: hedging and would rather, had better, may as well (reading only).

paras: It seems that the pump stopped at night. The engineer stated that he had checked it at midnight. More often than not, a pump stops because of a blocked filter.
The chief engineer would rather change the filter today than wait for the port. The crew had better check the other pumps too, and they may as well clean the tank at the same time.

quiz.q: It seems that the pump stopped at night. Is the writer sure?
The chief engineer would rather change the filter today than wait for the port. What does he prefer?
The crew had better check the other pumps too. What does it mean?
opts: The crew should check the other pumps.
The crew checked the pumps in the past.
The crew prefer the other pumps.

grammar_tip_lead: A hedge like it would appear that or it seems that shows that the writer is not sure. Would rather is a preference, had better is strong advice and may as well means there is no reason not to. You only need to read them and see how sure the writer is.

teacher.s1: Abertura (1 min): Aula no NIVEL NOVO (pedido da professora em 28/09): texto mais curto, frases simples, glossario na tela, 1 listening so e as respostas por ESCRITO. A prova e 100% leitura. Hedges e os modais de conselho hoje sao para LER, nao para produzir.
teacher.s2: Homework check + warm-up (4 min): Ela le UMA linha da ordem operacional que escreveu e escolhe um chip. Uma frase basta. Linha sem prazo: aponte sem corrigir o resto.
teacher.s3: Provocacao (3 min): Ela escolhe A ou B. Espere 5 segundos. Resposta: A (so a primeira e finding). Depois pergunte, com opcoes: the third sentence, is it a fact or what a person said? (What a person said.)
teacher.s4: Objetivo (1 min): Leia as tres missoes. Diga: today you answer in writing.
teacher.s5: Transicao vocab (1 min): Diga: Ten words of an inquiry. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s6: Vocab reveal 1-4 (4 min): negligence, testimony, investigation, finding. NAO traduza. CCQ com opcoes: If the witness is wrong, is it still testimony, yes or no? (Yes.)
teacher.s7: Vocab reveal 5-7 (4 min): recommendation, contributing factor, root cause. CCQ com opcoes: Without the root cause, does the event happen, yes or no? (No.)
teacher.s8: Vocab reveal 8-10 (4 min): corrective action, witness, sequence of events. CCQ com opcoes: Is a corrective action before or after the event? (After.)
teacher.s9: Consolidate (3 min): Ela liga os pares sozinha. Ajude so se ela pedir.
teacher.s10: Transicao leitura (1 min): Diga: This text is about how accidents are written. O proximo slide e o de TAREFA: a pergunta ANTES do texto.
teacher.s11: Leitura (7 min): Leitura silenciosa. Mostre o GLOSSARIO antes. Releitura de frase e normal. Se ela travar numa palavra fora do glossario, de um sinonimo simples em ingles.
teacher.s12: Gist (2 min): Ela escolhe a opcao e ESCREVE a linha que prova. Resposta: (c). A (a) e o assunto aparente, nao o que o texto faz.
teacher.s13: True or False (5 min): Ela responde as cinco e escreve a linha que prova cada uma. A 2 decide a aula: it would appear that NAO e finding.
teacher.s14: Transicao gramatica (1 min): Diga: The small words that show how sure the writer is. You only need to read them. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s15: Grammar discovery (6 min): Peca que ela ESCREVA o exemplo 1 sem o hedge e diga se e a mesma afirmacao. Depois o exemplo 3 com prefer. So entao clique Reveal the Rule. CCQ com opcoes: It would appear that X: is X sure, or only probable? (Only probable.)
teacher.s16: Practice (4 min): Ela escreve a versao simples ANTES de clicar. Aceite qualquer versao simples correta.
teacher.s17: Spot the error (3 min): A primeira erra de SENTIDO (o hedge nao da certeza). As outras erram de FORMA: to depois de would rather e had better, -ing depois de may as well.
teacher.s18: Transicao equivalencia (1 min): Diga: Same method, other words. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s19: Como a prova esconde (3 min): Leia os quatro pares com ela. O primeiro e o mais perigoso: os dois lados sao hedges. The valve was closed NAO seria equivalente.
teacher.s20: Equivalencia (4 min): Ela liga os pares. Ajude so depois de 5 segundos.
teacher.s21: Complete (4 min): Uma lacuna por vez. As oito respostas estao no banco de palavras.
teacher.s22: Quick fire POR ESCRITO (6 min): Ela escreve a resposta de cada uma no chat ou no papel, e so depois voces abrem as dicas. A primeira ensina o procedimento: procure o hedge na pagina.
teacher.s23: Transicao (1 min): Diga: One recording, then you write. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s24: Listening (5 min): O UNICO listening da aula (pedido da professora). LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar. Primeira vez em 0.75x, segunda em 1x. A frase It is honest about how much I know e a definicao de hedge: volte a ela.
teacher.s25: Writing (5 min): Ela escreve tres frases sobre a investigadora, uma por inicio. Corrija por escrito so o essencial (verbo e palavra tecnica). Depois clique Show a Model Answer.
teacher.s26: Escrita guiada (5 min): Quatro frases com os inicios. Conte quantos hedges ela usa certo, sem exigir.
teacher.s27: Escrita semi-livre (5 min): Para cada frase, S ou H e as palavras que decidem. Ela nao pode responder de memoria: tem de COPIAR as palavras da pagina.
teacher.s28: Producao (4 min): Ela ESCREVE duas findings e dois hedges e depois LE em voz alta. Esse e o unico momento de fala da fase: curto e com roteiro.
teacher.s29: Transicao wrap-up (1 min): Diga: Let us see what you can do now.
teacher.s30: Survival card (3 min): Cinco frases do texto. Toque e peca repeticao, uma vez cada. Would rather sai quase colado na fala: e assim que ela vai ouvir.
teacher.s31: Checklist (2 min): Leia cada item em voz alta. Os 5 checks fecham a aula e acendem o stamp.
teacher.s32: Encerramento (2 min): Diga: Lesson 9 complete, Helena. HOMEWORK ORALMENTE, nunca escrito na tela: (1) pegar cinco frases de qualquer texto do programa e escrever ao lado F (finding), H (hedge) ou T (testimony); (2) reescrever tres frases dela mesma com it would appear that. AVISO: a proxima aula e SIMULADO do bloco 2, com DOIS textos. Proxima aula: Block 2 Full Simulation.
teacher.s25b: Writing: certo ou nao (5 min): Uma finding, um hedge e um testemunho sobre o MESMO fato. Se ela misturar, pergunte: is the report sure here, yes or no? Depois clique Show a Model Answer e compare.
